cards.title: Design for Breakdowns
cards.body: Observe the opportunity in front of you and intentionally design how it would go wrong.
cards.note: Focus on errors, misunderstandings, misuse, and opportunities of abandonment.

cards.title: Make It Strange
cards.body: Take a familiar assumption and make it unfamiliar. What changes when the obvious rule, role, scale, or sequence is inverted?
cards.note: Push past the first clever answer.

cards.title: Borrow From Elsewhere
cards.body: Find a useful pattern in another place, discipline, culture, or living system. Translate its logic into the opportunity in front of you.
cards.note: Explain what you are borrowing and why.

cards.title: Make a Rough Version
cards.body: Turn the thought into something you can see, hear, touch, or walk through in the next ten minutes.
cards.note: It can be incomplete, awkward, or made from whatever is nearby.

cards.title: Act It Out
cards.body: Put the idea into motion. Show what happens before, during, and after the moment you are exploring.
cards.note: Use bodies, objects, words, or a simple sequence.

cards.title: Remove a Resource
cards.body: Try to make the idea without one resource, feature, habit, or permission that currently feels essential.
cards.note: Let the constraint produce a new direction.

cards.title: Look at the Edge
cards.body: Focus on the person, condition, or context furthest from the assumed centre. What does it reveal?
cards.note: Treat the edge as a source of insight, not an exception.

cards.title: Find the Friction
cards.body: Notice where effort, confusion, waiting, silence, or repetition gathers. What might that friction be telling you?
cards.note: Stay with the detail before jumping to a solution.

cards.title: Listen for the Unsaid
cards.body: What is being assumed, avoided, normalised, or left unspoken in this situation?
cards.note: Write down the quiet signal that usually gets missed.

cards.title: Argue the Opposite
cards.body: Make the strongest case for the opposite of your current direction. What becomes visible when you reverse your position?
cards.note: You do not have to agree with the argument.

cards.title: Design for Misuse
cards.body: Imagine the idea is misunderstood, repurposed, or used in an unintended way. What happens next?
cards.note: Look for risks, opportunities, and unexpected dignity.

cards.title: Stress the System
cards.body: Push the idea until it meets its limits: more people, less time, higher stakes, or a different setting.
cards.note: Notice what breaks and what proves resilient.

cards.title: Jump Ten Years
cards.body: Imagine this opportunity has become ordinary ten years from now. What does a normal day look and feel like?
cards.note: Describe one small detail that makes the future believable.

cards.title: Change the Scale
cards.body: Explore the same opportunity at a radically different scale: tiny enough to hold, or large enough to reshape a system.
cards.note: Make one intimate version and one systemic version.

cards.title: What If It Were a Ritual?
cards.body: Imagine the idea as a repeated ritual rather than a one-off intervention. What would people do, and what would it mean?
cards.note: Consider rhythm, roles, symbols, and belonging.
